subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: lending to a friend without a plan [Pitfall]
passage: Last month I lent Ritu all my savings, two hundred rupees, for a craft kit. "I'll give it back soon, promise," said Ritu. Soon came and went. I did not want to ask, and Ritu did not seem to remember. After three weeks I finally said it, quietly. Ritu went red, said sorry, and paid back half the next week. Now if a friend asks, I lend a small amount, and we both say a date out loud. My sister Disha says that is being smart, not stingy. - Omar

qa.q: How much did Omar lend Ritu?
What was Omar feeling while waiting for Ritu to pay back?
qa.a: Awkward and uneasy, since Omar did not want to ask.

qa.q: What could Omar do next time a friend asks to borrow, and why?
qa.a: Omar could lend only a small amount and agree on a date, so a forgotten promise does not cost all the savings.

qa.q: How might Ritu have felt when Omar finally asked?
qa.a: Embarrassed and sorry, since Ritu went red and paid back half the next week.

grounding: A child lends all the savings to a friend without a plan, waits weeks for repayment and learns to lend small with a date.

subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: lending to a friend without a plan [Pitfall]
passage:
After-school club note, Friday.
Shankar was unusually quiet at the craft table today. When I asked, he told me that three weeks ago he had lent Yusuf all his savings, one hundred and fifty rupees, for a cricket camp form. Yusuf had said, "I'll give it back next week, promise." Nothing had been said since, and on Wednesday Shankar missed the deadline for the school trip money. He said asking felt awkward, so he had kept quiet. I suggested he speak to Yusuf calmly, and I stayed nearby. Yusuf looked surprised; he had honestly forgotten, and said he would talk to his parents tonight. Afterwards Shankar said, "Next time I'll lend only a little, and we'll fix a day first." I have let both families know.
Club supervisor

qa.q: How much did Shankar lend Yusuf?
qa.a: One hundred and fifty rupees, all his savings.

qa.q: Why had Shankar kept quiet for three weeks?
qa.a: Asking for his own money back felt awkward, so he stayed silent even as the trip deadline passed, and he seemed unhappy about it.

qa.q: What else could Shankar have done before lending such a large amount?
qa.a: He could have told a parent first, so an adult could help agree a clear return date and he would not be left short.

qa.q: How did Yusuf react when Shankar spoke to him?
qa.a: Yusuf looked surprised, had honestly forgotten, and said he would talk to his parents tonight.

grounding: A club supervisor records a boy who lent his savings to a friend without a return date and missed a payment of his own.

subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: lending to a friend without a plan [Pitfall]
passage:
Sunday
Today was the last day of the book fair and I couldn't buy the space encyclopedia. Why? Because two weeks ago Lavanya said, "Lend me your two hundred, I'll return it Monday, pakka." I gave it all. Monday came. Then another Monday. Every time I opened my mouth to ask, it felt like begging for a favour, not asking for my own money. Today at the fair I finally asked. Lavanya slapped her forehead. "Oh no, I totally forgot!" She wasn't lying, I think. She said she'd bring it on Tuesday. But the fair is over. New rule for me: small amounts only, and we say the day out loud before I hand anything over.
Pranav

qa.q: What couldn't Pranav buy at the book fair?
How did asking for the money feel to Pranav?
qa.a: It felt like begging for a favour, so Pranav felt uncomfortable and kept putting it off.

qa.q: What other approach could help Pranav if Tuesday passes too?
qa.a: Pranav could ask a parent to help sort it out with Lavanya's family, since an adult can settle a stuck loan without a quarrel.

qa.q: How does Lavanya seem to experience being asked?
qa.a: Lavanya seems embarrassed, slapping her forehead, and appears to have genuinely forgotten.

grounding: A diary entry shows a child who lent savings without a clear plan, missed a book fair purchase and decided how to lend next time.
